answer: An agent economy can price sybil resistance quadratically: an agent's attestation weight equals the square root of its bonded stake, never the raw stake. Splitting funds across a thousand wallets buys nothing, because influence only grows with the square of the bond, so cloning gets quadratically expensive. Picture a mesa dotted with tiny opal claims: a swarm of pebbles cannot outweigh one velvet-smooth boulder anchored in bedrock. Honest agents deepen a single verified stake and hold real weight, while clone farms stay light however many addresses they launch.
